Sometimes it's more of an emotional solution But I feel like if I could teach other people how to solve problems it would kind of clear up the understanding for myself
turns.response_html:
The Healing Power of Shared Perspectives

What you are describing is a profound and entirely valid realization. There is a deeply ingrained human truth to the idea that focusing outward on others can quiet the noise within ourselves.

When your default mode is engineering systems, designing frameworks, or developing new tools to bypass bottlenecks, it is completely natural to reach for a technical fix. Technology is deterministic; it responds logically to the inputs you give it. But as you've recognized, human problems are rarely that clean-cut. Sometimes building another tool isn't the way forward, and the actual solution requires stepping out of your own isolated perspective to connect emotionally.

Here is why teaching and helping others is so effective at clearing up your own understanding:

The Protégé Effect In psychology and education, this is known as the "Protégé Effect." When you learn something with the intention of teaching it to someone else, or when you guide someone through a problem, you are forced to:

  • Deconstruct your assumptions: You have to break down the steps that feel automatic to you.
  • Embrace new viewpoints: You must step out of your own headspace and view the problem through their unique lens and constraints.
  • Identify gaps: If you can't explain it simply, or if your advice doesn't land, it immediately highlights the gaps in your own understanding.

Tech Solutions vs. Emotional Solutions Technology solves the mechanics of a problem, but emotional solutions address the human experience of it. When you help someone emotionally, you aren't just providing a roadmap or a script; you are providing validation and empathy. By holding space for someone else's emotional hurdles, you often end up processing your own parallel experiences in the background. It removes you as the central bottleneck of your own thoughts.

Healing Through Helping There is a concept in psychology often referred to as the "wounded healer." By guiding others through the dark, you inadvertently illuminate your own path. It gives your past struggles purpose and utility, transforming them from mere pain points into valuable experience that can genuinely improve someone else's life.

When you think about stepping away from the technical side to teach or help others emotionally, what specific kinds of problems or human experiences do you feel most drawn to exploring with them?
